Now I have a clear picture. The items in this batch are about EVM/execution layer concerns (ECDSA transaction signing, EIP-7883 ModExp gas), but Prysm is a consensus layer client that only passes raw transaction bytes to/from the execution layer engine (via the Engine API). Prysm does NOT:
1. Verify individual ECDSA transaction signatures
2. Implement EVM precompile gas calculations (ModExp/EIP-2565/EIP-7883)
3. Implement transaction type signing hash computation

These are responsibilities of the execution layer client (e.g., go-ethereum/geth). Prysm only handles the raw bytes opaquely.
